title: 1985 AMC 8 Problem 22
statement: Assume every \(7\)-digit whole number is a possible telephone number except those that begin with \(0\) or \(1.\) What fraction of telephone numbers begin with \(9\) and end with \(0?\)

solutions.text:
The first digit is one of \(8\) allowed digits (\(2\) through \(9\)), so \(\dfrac18\) of the numbers begin with \(9.\) The last digit is any of \(10\) digits, so \(\dfrac{1}{10}\) end in \(0.\)

These conditions are independent, so the fraction is \(\dfrac18 \cdot \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1}{80}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B .
hints: The first digit can be any of \(2\) through \(9,\) which is \(8\) choices
Multiply the fraction of telephone numbers that begin with \(9\) by the fraction that end in \(0\)
